title: MASAKADO
subtitle: the grave Tokyo is afraid to move
source: Masakado-ki; Kubizuka, Otemachi, Tokyo (Ministry of Finance deaths 1920s, 1940 lightning fire, 2020 relocation)

lines.say: [nervous] Kon... why is there a tiny grave in the middle of Tokyo?
cap: Kon... why is there a {o:tiny grave}

lines.say: [sly] Because everyone who tried to move it... died.
cap: Because everyone who tried to move it...

lines.say: [shocked] DIED?!
[storytelling] A thousand years ago, a samurai named Taira no Masakado rebelled against the emperor. He even crowned himself the New Emperor.
cap: A thousand years ago, a samurai named
He even crowned himself the {o:New Emperor}.

lines.say: Legend says his body was hard as iron. Except one spot. His temple. In the year nine-forty, an arrow found it.
cap: Legend says his body was {o:hard as iron}.

lines.say: [ominous] They cut off his head, and put it on display in Kyoto. But it never rotted. Its eyes stayed open. And every night, it screamed.
cap: and put it on display in {o:Kyoto}.

lines.say: [furious] [shouting] WHERE IS MY BODY?! BRING IT HERE! I WILL FIGHT AGAIN!
[intense] Then one night, the head rose into the sky, glowing, and flew east. All the way home.
[screaming] A FLYING HEAD?!
It crashed down in a little village. Today, that village is the center of Tokyo. They buried it right where it fell.
cap: It crashed down in a little village.
They buried it right where it fell.

lines.say: [darkly] After the great earthquake of nineteen twenty-three, the Ministry of Finance built offices right on top of it.
cap: built offices {r:right on top of it}.

lines.say: Within a few years, fourteen officials were dead. Including the Finance Minister himself.
[whispering] ...Coincidence?
[smug] In nineteen forty, exactly one thousand years after his death, lightning struck the Ministry. It burned to the ground.
cap: exactly {r:one thousand years} after his death,

lines.say: After the war, soldiers tried to bulldoze the grave for a parking lot. The story goes, the bulldozer flipped. And the driver died.
cap: After the war, soldiers tried to {o:bulldoze} the grave

lines.say: [whispering] Even today, some workers in those towers won't sit with their backs to it.
cap: Even today, some workers in those towers
won't sit with their {r:backs} to it.

lines.say: [nervous] Okay. So nobody EVER touches it.
[casually] Well... in twenty twenty, they moved the stone for repairs.
[nervous] ...And?
[ominous] That same week, an earthquake shook Ibaraki. Where his body is said to be buried.
cap: Where his {r:body} is said to be buried.

lines.say: [panicking] NOPE. I'm leaving. Bye.
[whispering] Mio... never turn your back on him.
[whispering] [menacing] Where... is my body?
